boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of California-Irvine
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food destinations with currently published late hours in Irvine and immediately beside UCI.

cards.title: In-N-Out Burger on Campus Drive
cards.subtitle: 4115 Campus Drive — on campus, across from UCI
cards.notes: Use the Campus Drive location when you need a late food stop close to campus; confirm whether you want dine-in or drive-thru before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A UCI-adjacent restaurant with published service until 1 a.m. most nights and 1:30 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: In-N-Out lists this 4115 Campus Drive restaurant as “On Campus; across from UCI,” with normal hours to 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 1:30 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Published normal hours: 10:30 a.m.–1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday; 10:30 a.m.–1:30 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Campus Drive
cards.subtitle: 4101 Campus Drive, Irvine
cards.notes: Check the location page before heading out, then use the Campus Drive address for a late, straightforward food pickup near UCI.
cards.short_summary: A Campus Drive Taco Bell whose official dinner page lists it as open 24 hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official page for 4101 Campus Drive identifies the Irvine location and lists Tuesday as open 24 hours.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell Dinner — 4101 Campus Drive, Irvine
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists the restaurant as open 24 hours; verify same-day service details before departure.

cards.title: Del Taco on Irvine Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 4780 Irvine Boulevard, Irvine
cards.notes: Keep this Irvine Boulevard address handy for a late pickup; the official location page publishes round-the-clock store hours for every day.
cards.short_summary: A north Irvine option with official 24-hour daily store hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Del Taco’s official page for 4780 Irvine Blvd. states that the location is open 24 hours every day of the week.
cards.access_notes: Official store-hours table lists “Open 24 hours” Sunday through Saturday.

cards.title: Denny's on Sand Canyon Avenue
cards.subtitle: 14962 Sand Canyon Avenue, Irvine
cards.notes: Use the official hours shown for the day you plan to go; it is a practical sit-down or pickup option when other kitchens have closed.
cards.short_summary: A Sand Canyon diner with published hours reaching nearly midnight every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny’s lists its 14962 Sand Canyon Avenue store with hours to 11:44 p.m. or 11:58 p.m., depending on the day.
cards.access_notes: Official current listing shows closing at 11:44 p.m. Monday–Wednesday and Sunday, and 11:58 p.m. Thursday–Saturday.

cards.title: Super Yummy in Corporate Park
cards.subtitle: 92 Corporate Park, Suite B, Irvine
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s own site to confirm the 2 a.m. closing time, then plan your visit around the listed Corporate Park address.
cards.short_summary: An Irvine Asian-fusion restaurant publishing daily service until 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Super Yummy’s official menu page lists 92 Corporate Park, Suite B, Irvine and hours of 9:30 a.m.–2 a.m. Monday through Sunday.
cards.source_title: Super Yummy Irvine — Menu and Hours
cards.access_notes: Official page lists daily hours: 9:30 a.m.–2 a.m.

cards.title: Jack in the Box on Burt Road
cards.subtitle: 6565 Burt Road, Irvine
cards.notes: For late drive-thru service, use the Burt Road location page and note that its lobby and drive-thru have different published closing times.
cards.short_summary: A south Irvine drive-thru with official service until 3 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Jack in the Box lists its 6565 Burt Road drive-thru as open until 3 a.m.; the lobby is listed until 11 p.m.
cards.source_title: Jack in the Box — 6565 Burt Road, Irvine
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru hours through 3 a.m.; lobby hours through 11 p.m.

cards.title: Wendy's on Culver Drive
cards.subtitle: 14386 Culver Drive, Irvine
cards.notes: Use this Culver Drive location when its later nightly schedule fits; the official page lists the same late hours for restaurant and drive-thru.
cards.short_summary: A Culver Drive location with official hours as late as 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists 14386 Culver Drive open until 1 a.m. Monday–Tuesday and 2 a.m. Wednesday–Sunday, for both restaurant and drive-thru.
cards.access_notes: Official restaurant and drive-thru hours: until 1 a.m. Monday–Tuesday and 2 a.m. Wednesday–Sunday.

cards.title: Wendy's on Technology Drive
cards.subtitle: 63 Technology Drive, Irvine
cards.notes: For a midnight option south of campus, check the official location page and use its listed Technology Drive address for restaurant or drive-thru service.
cards.short_summary: A Technology Drive restaurant publishing midnight closing every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists 63 Technology Drive open until 12 a.m. daily for both restaurant and drive-thru.
cards.access_notes: Official restaurant and drive-thru hours both run until 12 a.m. daily.

cards.title: Eureka! on Campus Drive
cards.subtitle: 4143 Campus Drive, Irvine
cards.notes: If you want a seated late dinner, check the restaurant’s current day-specific hours and use the Campus Drive address near the university.
cards.short_summary: A Campus Drive restaurant whose official location page lists midnight Friday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Eureka!’s official Irvine location page lists 4143 Campus Drive and Friday hours from 11 a.m. to 12 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists Friday hours until 12 a.m.; consult that page for the selected day’s current hours.

cards.title: Del Taco on Barranca Parkway
cards.subtitle: 4820 Barranca Parkway, Irvine
cards.notes: Use the official locator for same-day availability, then follow the listed Barranca Parkway address for a late food pickup in Irvine.
cards.short_summary: A separately named Irvine Del Taco location listed by the chain’s official locator.
cards.evidence_claim: Del Taco’s official Irvine location page lists a nearby restaurant at 4820 Barranca Pkwy, Irvine, CA 92604; the chain presents it as an Irvine location for ordering and directions.
cards.access_notes: The official locator identifies the 4820 Barranca Parkway location; confirm its exact current closing time on its individual location page before traveling.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UCI places for studying, connecting, recharging, recreation, and campus programs, each supported by a direct university or library source.

cards.title: Aldrich Park
cards.subtitle: UC Irvine campus green at the center of campus life
cards.notes: Use the paths between classes or pause on the lawn before your next stop; campus life resources describe UCI as centered around this park.
cards.short_summary: The central green space that links much of the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Irvine describes its campus life as centered around Aldrich Park.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; follow posted campus rules and event restrictions.

cards.title: UCI Student Center
cards.subtitle: Student Center · Ring Road area
cards.notes: Make this a practical between-class stop for study, services, and campus programs; the building lists quiet spaces and reservable rooms.
cards.short_summary: A central building for study rooms, student services, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The UCI Student Center provides quiet places to sit, work, or read and rooms available for reservation.
cards.source_title: UC Irvine Student Center & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Building hours are listed as 7:00 a.m.–midnight daily, excluding university holidays.

cards.title: Courtyard Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: First floor, UCI Student Center, near the Meditation Space
cards.notes: Reserve a group room when you need whiteboards, power, and Wi-Fi; reservations use a current UCInetID and depend on availability.
cards.short_summary: Reservable Student Center study rooms with useful group-work amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Courtyard Study Lounge has reservable study rooms plus Wi-Fi, whiteboards, power, vending machines, and restrooms.
cards.source_title: Book a Study Room Online | UC Irvine Student Center & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7:30 a.m.–11:30 p.m.; study rooms are for UCI students and require reservations.

cards.title: Commuter Lounge
cards.subtitle: Information Center, first-floor entrance of the UCI Student Center
cards.notes: Use the seating, outlets, Wi-Fi, microwave, and refrigerator during a long gap; ask in person about a same-day locker if needed.
cards.short_summary: A Student Center lounge designed for students spending long days on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Commuter Lounge offers lounge seating, power outlets, Wi-Fi, a microwave, refrigerator, and day-use lockers.
cards.source_title: Commuter Lounge | UC Irvine Student Center & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Lounge hours are Monday–Friday 7:30 a.m.–8:00 p.m. and weekends 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; lockers are day-of for UCI students.

cards.title: Cross-Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: Ring Road, across from Starbucks and Aldrich Hall
cards.notes: Check the center’s programs or sit down with peers in an affirming campus setting; student organizations can pursue room reservations through its process.
cards.short_summary: A Ring Road center for identity exploration, community, and student-led programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cross-Cultural Center says its space supports students in exploring social identities, building relationships, and promoting lifelong learning.
cards.access_notes: The center lists Spring 2026 building hours as daily, 8:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m.; check the site for quarter updates.

cards.entity_name: Center for Black Cultures, Resources and Research
cards.title: Center for Black Cultures, Resources and Research
cards.subtitle: UCI Student Center, Level 1, Room B116
cards.notes: Visit the Student Center location to learn about its culturally supportive programming and resources, or check its own site before attending an activity.
cards.short_summary: A Student Center cultural resource space supporting Black student thriving.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI states that the Center for Black Cultures, Resources and Research provides a safe, vibrant, inclusive, culturally supportive space where Black students can thrive.
cards.source_title: Services | UC Irvine Student Center & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Located in the Student Center at Level 1, Room B116; consult the center for programming and access details.

cards.title: UCI DREAM Center
cards.subtitle: RISE Suite, UCI Student Center Level 4, Room G458
cards.notes: Use this Student Center base to find programming and support related to immigration policy; contact the center for current services and gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A Student Center space serving people affected by immigration policy.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI describes the DREAM Center as serving those impacted by immigration policy through systemic change, personal growth, collective healing, and visible change.
cards.source_title: Services | UC Irvine Student Center & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Located in the RISE Suite at Level 4, Room G458; contact dream@uci.edu for current details.

cards.title: Langson Library
cards.subtitle: UC Irvine Libraries · central campus
cards.notes: Choose the third floor when collaborating with a group, or use the designated quiet zones when you need a lower-noise study setting.
cards.short_summary: A major UCI library with group areas, quiet zones, and reservable study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries identifies Langson's third floor as a group study area and lists quiet-study zones in its basement, fourth floor, and Special Collections.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms may be booked by current UCI students, staff, and faculty; check library hours and room availability before going.

cards.title: Science Library
cards.subtitle: UC Irvine Libraries · Science Library
cards.notes: Use the open study seating or reserve a study room for focused group work; keep conversations out of the fourth- and sixth-floor quiet zones.
cards.short_summary: A large library study setting with reservable rooms and designated quiet floors.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries states that the Science Library has over 30 study rooms, 2,000 individual study spaces, and quiet-study zones on floors four and six.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms may be booked by current UCI students, staff, and faculty; verify library hours and reservations online.

cards.title: Gateway Study Center
cards.subtitle: Across from Langson Library · 106 Gateway Study Center
cards.notes: Check the Study Space Locator for a reservable room, or look for SOAR Center study-support programming during the quarter and finals period.
cards.short_summary: A study-center building across from Langson with reservable rooms and SOAR programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries states that Gateway Study Center is across from Langson Library and offers 13 reservable study rooms; SOAR is located at 106 Gateway Study Center.
cards.access_notes: Library information says Gateway has 13 study rooms reservable through the Study Space Locator; it is open 24 hours during 10th and Finals weeks.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten verified UCI and Irvine places for studying, browsing art, and taking a low-key walk without admission.

cards.title: Walk through University Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Claire Trevor School of the Arts, UCI
cards.notes: Meet by the gallery entrance, take a self-guided lap, then compare one work each before heading to the next nearby gallery.
cards.short_summary: A free art stop in the Arts Plaza galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: University Art Gallery is one of UCI's University Art Galleries, where admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visit | University Art Galleries | Department of Art | Claire Trevor School of the Arts
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, noon–6 p.m.; hours are subject to change. Campus parking requires a permit.

cards.title: Browse the CAC Gallery
cards.subtitle: Contemporary Arts Center, UCI
cards.notes: Use this gallery as a calm conversation stop: look independently first, then regroup and trade observations about the exhibition.
cards.short_summary: Free contemporary-art viewing at the Claire Trevor School of the Arts.
cards.evidence_claim: Contemporary Arts Center Gallery is part of UCI's University Art Galleries, whose admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visit | University Art Galleries | Department of Art | Claire Trevor School of the Arts
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, noon–6 p.m.; hours are subject to change. Campus parking requires a permit.

cards.title: Visit Room Gallery
cards.subtitle: Art Culture and Technology Building, UCI
cards.notes: Pair a quick Room Gallery visit with a short walk around the arts buildings, leaving time to read wall text or artist materials.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery stop in UCI's Art Culture and Technology building.
cards.evidence_claim: Room Gallery is part of UCI's University Art Galleries, whose admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visit | University Art Galleries | Department of Art | Claire Trevor School of the Arts
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, noon–6 p.m.; hours are subject to change. Campus parking requires a permit.

cards.entity_name: UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art
cards.title: See California art at Langson IMCA
cards.subtitle: 18881 Von Karman Avenue, Irvine
cards.notes: Plan a shared museum circuit through the current galleries, then pause in the reading lounge to talk about a work that caught your eye.
cards.short_summary: Free public museum admission in Irvine.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art states that admission is always free.
cards.source_title: UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; confirm current exhibitions before going.

cards.title: Settle into Langson Library
cards.subtitle: UCI main campus
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a quiet work session, browse a shelf between tasks, or use the on-site collections before taking a study break.
cards.short_summary: On-site library use is available at no cost.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries identifies Langson Library as a campus library and says on-site books, journals, newspapers, and other resources are available at no cost.
cards.source_title: Suggestions for Successful Visits | UC Irvine Libraries
cards.access_notes: The library welcomes the general public; parking, printing, and photocopying have fees. Check current building hours.

cards.title: Browse Science Library together
cards.subtitle: UCI main campus
cards.notes: Choose a table for a low-cost study hang, then browse science titles or periodicals on-site when you need a focused break.
cards.short_summary: Free on-site access to a UCI library's resources.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries identifies Science Library as a campus library and says on-site books, journals, newspapers, and other resources are available at no cost.
cards.source_title: Suggestions for Successful Visits | UC Irvine Libraries
cards.access_notes: The library welcomes the general public; parking, printing, and photocopying have fees. Check current building hours.

cards.title: Request archival material on-site
cards.subtitle: UC Irvine Libraries
cards.notes: Pick a local-history or campus-history question together, then ask library staff how to consult relevant archival materials in person.
cards.short_summary: Explore UCI archival materials without an admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Irvine Libraries says special collections and archival materials are available for on-site use at no cost.
cards.source_title: Suggestions for Successful Visits | UC Irvine Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use is on-site; ask staff about handling and access procedures. Parking, printing, and photocopying may cost extra.

cards.title: Take a self-guided library exhibit lap
cards.subtitle: UC Irvine Libraries
cards.notes: Choose an exhibit location, read the introductory panel, and give each person time to find one detail worth discussing afterward.
cards.short_summary: Public, self-guided library exhibits with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Irvine Libraries exhibits are self-guided, open to the public, and available at no cost during regular library hours.
cards.source_title: Exhibit Visitor Information | UCI Exhibits Site
cards.access_notes: Available during regular library hours; check the exhibit site for current locations and dates. Campus parking requires a permit.

cards.title: Research side by side on a library computer
cards.subtitle: UC Irvine Libraries
cards.notes: Use an on-site computer to look up a topic, scan a short source, and share a few useful finds without needing to buy anything.
cards.short_summary: No-cost on-site computer access for visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Irvine Libraries says computers with internet access are available for on-site use at no cost.
cards.source_title: Suggestions for Successful Visits | UC Irvine Libraries
cards.access_notes: Visitor Wi-Fi access is limited; computers are listed as available on-site at no cost. Check building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the UCI Arboretum gardens
cards.subtitle: UCI North Campus, near Campus Drive and Jamboree Road
cards.notes: Take the paths at an unhurried pace and use the plant collections as prompts for photos, sketches, or a quiet outdoor catch-up.
cards.short_summary: A botanical-garden walk with documented free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Irvine reported that admission and parking at the UCI Arboretum are free.
cards.source_title: Arboretum is no garden-variety greenhouse – UC Irvine News
cards.access_notes: The Arboretum's access and open days can change; verify its current public hours before making the trip.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented UCI study settings spanning quiet library floors, reservable rooms, technology-equipped spaces, and the Student Center.

cards.entity_name: Langson Library Fourth Floor Quiet Study Zone
cards.title: Langson Library Fourth Floor Quiet Study Zone
cards.subtitle: Langson Library · fourth floor
cards.notes: Bring materials for focused individual work, silence your phone, and keep conversations outside because this floor is a designated Quiet Study Zone.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet floor in Langson Library for individual reading and writing.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries designates Langson Library's fourth floor as a Quiet Study Zone and directs users to turn off cell phones and take conversations outside.
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours apply; UCI Libraries lists this as a Quiet Study Zone.

cards.entity_name: Langson Library Basement Quiet Study Zone
cards.title: Langson Library Basement Quiet Study Zone
cards.subtitle: Langson Library · basement
cards.notes: Use this designated quiet zone for sustained reading or drafting; switch devices to silent and move any conversation outside the study area.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-study option below the main levels of Langson Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries lists the Langson Library basement among its designated Quiet Study Zones.
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours apply; phones should be off and conversations taken outside.

cards.entity_name: Langson Library Third Floor Study Areas
cards.title: Langson Library Third Floor Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Langson Library · third floor
cards.notes: Set up here when working with classmates or when a little background sound is workable; the library designates these areas for group study.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor group-study area where conversation is permitted.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries identifies Langson Library's third-floor study areas as a designated group-study area for students seeking background noise or group work.
cards.access_notes: Use the Study Space Locator to check availability; this is a group-study area rather than a quiet zone.

cards.entity_name: Langson Library Third Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Langson Library Third Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Langson Library · third floor
cards.notes: Reserve a room through the Study Space Locator before meeting; use the enclosed setup for a defined group session and clear out at reservation end.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group rooms in Langson Library with varying room sizes.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries states that Langson Library's third floor has group study rooms of various sizes and directs users to the Study Space Locator.
cards.access_notes: Reservations are required through the Study Space Locator; library study-room policies apply.

cards.title: Nordstrom Honors Study Room
cards.subtitle: Langson Library · fourth floor
cards.notes: Ask the Check Out Desk about entry before settling in; this fourth-floor room is specifically available for Honors students.
cards.short_summary: An Honors-student study room on Langson Library's fourth floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries says the Nordstrom Honors Study Room is on Langson Library's fourth floor and is available for Honors students through the Check Out Desk.
cards.access_notes: Available to Honors students; speak with a Check Out Desk staff member for use information.

cards.entity_name: Science Library Fourth Floor Quiet Study Zone
cards.title: Science Library Fourth Floor Quiet Study Zone
cards.subtitle: Science Library · fourth floor
cards.notes: Choose this floor for uninterrupted individual work, keep your phone off, and take conversations outside in line with the library's quiet-zone guidance.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study floor in Science Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries designates the fourth floor of Science Library as a Quiet Study Zone.
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours apply; phones should be off and conversations taken outside.

cards.entity_name: Science Library Sixth Floor Quiet Study Zone
cards.title: Science Library Sixth Floor Quiet Study Zone
cards.subtitle: Science Library · sixth floor
cards.notes: Use the sixth floor when you need a quiet individual-work setting; prepare materials before you arrive and keep conversations outside the zone.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study floor in Science Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries designates the sixth floor of Science Library as a Quiet Study Zone.
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours apply; phones should be off and conversations taken outside.

cards.title: Science Library Honors Study Room
cards.subtitle: Science Library · fifth floor
cards.notes: Confirm access with the Check Out Desk, then use the fifth-floor Honors room for a focused session with your course materials.
cards.short_summary: An Honors-student study room on the fifth floor of Science Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries lists an Honors Study Room on the fifth floor of Science Library and directs users to the Check Out Desk for information.
cards.access_notes: Speak to a Science Library Check Out Desk staff member for use information.

cards.title: MRC SL Room 173
cards.subtitle: Multimedia Resources Center · Science Library
cards.notes: Reserve SL 173 for a small project group that needs a whiteboard, desktop, projector, and HDMI-connected display; bring valid UCI identification.
cards.short_summary: A reservable MRC room equipped for collaborative media and presentation work.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Libraries describes MRC SL Room 173 as having a table, seven chairs, whiteboard, desktop, overhead projector, and flat-screen TV with HDMI cable.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to currently enrolled UCI students, faculty, and staff with valid UCI ID; reserve through the MRC study-space system.

cards.title: Courtyard Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: UCI Student Center
cards.notes: Reserve a study room online when your work benefits from campus Wi-Fi, a whiteboard, power, and nearby restrooms in the Student Center.
cards.short_summary: A Student Center study lounge with reservable rooms and practical work amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The UCI Student Center offers online study-room reservations for the Courtyard Study Lounge and lists campus Wi-Fi, whiteboards, power, and nearby restrooms.
cards.source_title: UC Irvine Student Center & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Reserve a study room online; the Student Center lists building hours of 7:00 a.m.–midnight daily, excluding university holidays.

cards.access_notes: Restaurant in University Center; verify current hours and ordering options with the restaurant.

cards.notes: Use the 4101 Campus Drive café for tacos, burritos, quesadillas, nachos, or nonalcoholic café beverages; check the current menu before ordering.

cards.title: In-N-Out Burger

cards.notes: Visit the Campus Drive location for a quick-casual burger meal, and check the restaurant’s current service details before you head out.
cards.short_summary: A Southern California burger stop at University Center.
cards.evidence_claim: University Center lists In-N-Out Burger at 4115 Campus Dr and describes it as offering hamburgers and other quick-casual fare.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant in University Center; verify current hours and ordering options with the restaurant.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UCI rituals, recurring campus celebrations, and Anteater symbols.

cards.title: Answer the Anteater war cry
cards.subtitle: UCI school-spirit tradition
cards.notes: Listen for “Zot!” at an Anteater event, then use the three-part call with the crowd rather than treating it as a generic mascot slogan.
cards.short_summary: UCI adopted the anteater’s “Zot!” sound as its rallying cry in October 1965.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Athletics identifies “Zot” as a war cry borrowed from the anteater in the B.C. comic strip and says the student campaign established it before the 1965 mascot election.
cards.access_notes: Use at public UCI spirit or athletics events; confirm each event’s entry policy separately.

cards.title: Learn the Rip ’Em Eaters hand sign
cards.subtitle: UCI Anteater gesture
cards.notes: Check the official illustration and try the hand sign at a game or campus gathering as a simple, no-equipment way to show Anteater affiliation.
cards.short_summary: The hand sign draws on an anteater’s defensive posture and is presented by UCI Athletics as a shared Anteater symbol.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Athletics says the Rip ’Em Eaters hand sign is based on an anteater’s defensive action and was established to give UCI students and alumni a shared sign of pride and camaraderie.
cards.access_notes: Appropriate for public campus and athletics settings.

cards.title: Trace the choice of the Anteater
cards.subtitle: UCI’s mascot tradition
cards.notes: Read the official election account before spotting Peter the Anteater at a public campus event; it explains why this mascot is central to UCI identity.
cards.short_summary: Students selected the Anteater in UCI’s 1965 mascot election.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Athletics reports that student-athletes and a fellow student organized the anteater campaign before the November 30, 1965 student election, in which the Anteater received 55.9 percent of the vote.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances vary by event; check the host event’s details.

cards.title: Join the Community Roots Festival
cards.subtitle: Formerly the Rainbow Festival
cards.notes: Use the Cross-Cultural Center schedule to find performances and organization booths, then take time to learn directly from participating campus communities.
cards.short_summary: Founded in 1984, this fall gathering continues the Cross-Cultural Center’s Rainbow Festival tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The UCI Cross-Cultural Center describes Community Roots Festival, formerly Rainbow Festival, as a longstanding tradition founded in 1984 with cultural performances, interactive booths and student-organization fundraising.
cards.source_title: Community Roots Festival | UC Irvine Cross-Cultural Center
cards.access_notes: See the Cross-Cultural Center page for the current year’s program and participation details.

cards.title: Remember Midnight Magic
cards.subtitle: Historic UCI basketball-season kickoff
cards.notes: Use the UCI archive to understand this basketball kickoff, then check current Athletics and student-event calendars before expecting a present-day edition.
cards.short_summary: UCI’s basketball-season celebration debuted as Midnight Magic in 1998 after earlier Anteater Basketball Bash events.
cards.evidence_claim: A UCI News traditions account states that Midnight Magic debuted in 1998 and became a yearly basketball-season celebration, typically featuring team introductions, scrimmages and skills contests.
cards.source_title: UCI traditions tutorial | UC Irvine News
cards.access_notes: Historical documentation; confirm whether a current edition is scheduled before visiting.

cards.title: Start with SPOP
cards.subtitle: Historic incoming-student orientation tradition
cards.notes: If you are an incoming student or supporter, use UCI’s current orientation information for eligibility and registration rather than relying on this historic format.
cards.short_summary: SPOP was documented by UCI as a summer orientation series introducing incoming students and parents to campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI News described SPOP as a longstanding summer orientation tradition in which incoming freshmen and parents learned about college life and students enrolled in classes.
cards.source_title: UCI traditions tutorial | UC Irvine News
cards.access_notes: Historical account; current orientation formats and registration may differ.

cards.title: Come back for UCI Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Anteater reunion and campus celebration
cards.notes: Follow the Student Alumni Association’s Homecoming information for the current program, and choose the family-friendly daytime activities that fit your visit.
cards.short_summary: The Student Alumni Association calls UCI Homecoming a long-standing tradition that brings Anteaters together for festivities.
cards.evidence_claim: The UCI Student Alumni Association lists UCI Homecoming among its annual events and describes it as a long-standing tradition bringing Anteaters together for festivities in the park.
cards.source_title: Student Alumni Association | UCI Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Consult the current Homecoming schedule and registration information before attending.

cards.title: Make MLK Day a day on
cards.subtitle: Anteater community-service tradition
cards.notes: Register through UCI Volunteer Programs when a service project is posted, and plan to take part in the reflection and community-service components together.
cards.short_summary: UCI Volunteer Programs frames MLK Jr. Day of Service as an Anteater tradition of community service.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Volunteer Programs states that MLK Jr. Day of Service is a tradition for Anteaters to continue Martin Luther King Jr.’s legacy through community service.
cards.source_title: Martin Luther King Jr. Day of Service | UCI Volunteer Programs
cards.access_notes: The official page includes Winter 2026 information; registration and project availability can change.

cards.title: Celebrate campus organizations
cards.subtitle: Annual UCI recognition ceremony
cards.notes: Review the nominees and ceremony details, then attend or support an eligible registered organization during the awards season if participation is open.
cards.short_summary: The Anteater Awards is an annual ceremony recognizing UCI registered campus organizations and volunteer programs.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI Campus Organizations calls the Anteater Awards an annual tradition recognizing achievements and contributions of its 600-plus registered campus organizations through a nominations-based ceremony.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists the 2026 ceremony for May 27; verify event access or RSVP requirements.

cards.title: Notice the anteater-nose mace
cards.subtitle: UCI commencement ceremonial tradition
cards.notes: At commencement, look for the mace at the front of the processional and read its official history before the ceremony begins.
cards.short_summary: A California-oak mace shaped like an anteater’s nose leads UCI commencement processions.
cards.evidence_claim: UCI’s commencement-program history states that the UCI Mace was first carried in 2000, is fashioned to resemble an anteater’s nose, and is carried by a distinguished alumnus or alumna to lead the commencement processional.
cards.source_title: Commencement Program 2020 | UCI Paul Merage School of Business
cards.access_notes: Ceremonial viewing is limited to commencement attendees and guests under current event rules.
